The owner, asked whether SEA and CLOUDS planning could start now rather than waiting on their port timing, said (13 Nov 2026): "On 2 use the fable planner like normal but you can bring that across when it makes sense." Lead's reading, to record as an assumption: planning starts now, and the owner leaves to this plan when the Broadsides Rust work is brought across, within docs/design/decisions/SEA-AND-CLOUD-PORT.md (module by module, no wholesale import, Broadsides untouched). The design review of CLOUDS at docs/evidence/CLOUDS/design-review.md asked for changes. Resolve its 4 Must Fix findings in the design and the plan. Its Suggestions are yours to take or leave; say which you took and why.

Revisit the CLOUDS design from first principles. The owner, 14 Nov 2026: "You can fully use everything in broadsides. But we should make sure that it aligns with the approach we want. But yes, you can copy that code out and reuse as is if it's useful." Then: "We can fully reuse anything from broadsides, but it's there as a resource where it's useful, it shouldn't dictate design." Then, on clouds: "So in broadsides you will find both a procedural cloud setup as well as pre-baked clouds. The idea being that we could support both those two sky types as well as a hybrid as needed by the game being built." And then: "That's the approach we were going with in broadsides that might not be the right approach here. The agent should look at that work from first principles and figure out how to design the best possible atmospheric system for the thrum game engine. Maybe that's a flexible set of cloud capabilities built from what we did in broadsides, maybe it isn't, but it should start from first principles." Lead's reading, to record as assumptions: the owner's last words govern; the existing CLOUDS design and docs/design/decisions/SEA-AND-CLOUD-PORT.md describe the Broadsides approach and are inputs to judge, not constraints; Broadsides code, shaders and assets may be copied and reused as is wherever the design you arrive at finds them useful, and Broadsides itself stays unmodified. Settle the best CLOUDS for the Thrum engine, keep or change the current design accordingly and say why, and update the port decision to match what you decide. SEA M1 is being built in a worktree now; if your design changes what it builds, say so plainly.

The owner, 14 Nov 2026, about the SEA module: "Please make sure the sea work is actually thinking about water as a whole. So puddles, rivers, water falls, streams, lakes, and more. We want something that's built cohesively." Earlier the same day: "The agent should look at that work from first principles and figure out how to design the best possible atmospheric system for the thrum game engine." SEA today plans only an open sea; inland water lives in older designs (docs/design/modules/WATER*.md, docs/design/decisions/E1-GPU-WATER.md) with no module planned. From first principles, design Thrum's water as one cohesive system covering every body of water a game needs, and settle how the modules, plan and build order carry it (renaming or splitting SEA if that is right). Treat the existing designs and Broadsides as evidence, not constraints. SEA M1 is being built in a worktree now; if your design changes what it builds, say so plainly.

That covered: a warning-only gate, an hourly verifier on main, `gpu: 2, chrome: 1`, BASELINE-GUARD re-planned, the rule and skill text updated, and accepting that an unintended image change can sit on main for about 2 hours.

Carry out, adjusted for 2.3.0:
- **T1a.** The exact-baselines gate in `./dev check` warns instead of refusing. Declare the verifier as a `Main-branch check` in ORCHESTRATE.md (every 1h; lock gpu; a timeout that fits the ~16 min run). Record a dated ruling in ARCHITECTURE.md's Exact baselines.
- **T1b.** The script now does the sentinel's shared run, retry, bisect and naming the culprit. Re-plan BASELINE-GUARD down to what remains Thrum's own (for example the verify command and the CPU ownership guard), and decide what happens to its in-flight M2 on branch build/baseline-guard.
- **Verifier items.** Open milestones carry about 116 items whose check runs `exact_baselines.py verify`. Changing `check` text resets progress, which `lock` and `reads` don't. Weigh repointing them at `python3 "$ORCHESTRATE_SCRIPT" main-check <name>` (no lock of its own) against having the verifier read the shared result. Pick the option that disturbs open branches least, and say why.
- **T2-T5,** as the report says. In T4, never nest gpu inside merge, and never hold a lock while waiting for a person.
- **T6.** Declare `Shared resources: gpu: 2, chrome: 1`; that capacity change is what ends most of the queueing. Give each item the lock its device needs for capacity. Use `gpu.alone` only for a run that needs the whole GPU, such as all its memory. It does not make timings trustworthy, because builders compiling elsewhere take no lock.
- **T9's timing policy is the timing fix.** Within a milestone, a timing item becomes a loose benchmark tripwire that catches a collapse. Precise numbers move to the module's last milestone, measured in one sitting with builders paused. Sweep the timing items to that line.
- **Fold T7-T8 in** where they're cheap; otherwise record them as later work.
